findings.finding: The FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guide of ~$220-230M (maintained 2026-08-05) needs H2 2026 EBITDA of $115-125M after H1 of $105.0M (Q1 $50.8M + Q2 $54.2M, down 5.4% from H1 2025's ~$111.0M); H2 2025 was $108.8M (Q3 $49.0M + Q4 $59.8M, the Q4 including a national-advertising-fund timing benefit), so even the low end requires H2 +5.7% and the midpoint +10% after a declining first half — a cut to the low end or below is the likelier guide outcome, though Q3's $49.0M year-ago comp is easy.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 (2025-11-05): EBITDA fell to $49.0M from $61.9M and management guided EBITDA to the low end of the range; adjusted EPS $0.73 vs ~$0.82-0.99 consensus — the stock still rose +3.5% (baseline). Q2 2025 (2025-08-06) -6.42%. The name has not reliably sold off on EBITDA disappointments.
findings.why_not_priced: The H1/H2 arithmetic is public but no preview found states it; if the market were pricing a guide cut the stock would not be +18.7% in 20 days into the print. Consensus EPS $0.97-1.06 vs $0.73 a year ago implies a sharp Q3 EBITDA rebound is already in estimates.
findings.independence: FY2025 EBITDA and Q4/Q3 2025 figures from separate releases: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/49754/000119312526068524/d108405dex991.htm and https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20251105411269/en/Dine-Brands-Global-Inc.-Reports-Third-Quarter-2025-Results. Shares the Q2 release with the Applebee's comp finding (different line).

findings.finding: Applebee's domestic comps ran +1.9% in Q1 and -1.8% in Q2 2026 (~0% YTD, the bottom of the 0-2% guide), Q3 laps +3.1% (its best quarter of 2025), and the closest casual-dining peer Chili's printed +10.1% comps on +6.4% traffic for the quarter to 2026-09-23 — a share-taking read that points to a soft Applebee's Q3 comp and pressure on the comp guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (Applebee's -1.8%, below guide; EPS $1.16 vs $1.24) bought +2.58%; Q1 2026 (Applebee's +1.9%) sold -3.52%. Applebee's comp surprises have not mapped cleanly to the reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: DIN rallied alongside Brinker's +13% day, which reads the Chili's print as a sector tailwind rather than as share taken from Applebee's; if the share-loss reading were priced DIN would have lagged on 10-28 rather than run +9.5% in five sessions. Management said early Q3 trends were 'encouraging' with May/June improving, which is the market's prior.
findings.independence: Applebee's comps from the company's Q1 and Q2 releases (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000049754/000119312526208752/d122809dex991.htm, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000049754/000119312526333848/d148591dex991.htm); Q3 2025 lap +3.1% from https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20251105411269/en/Dine-Brands-Global-Inc.-Reports-Third-Quarter-2025-Results. Net of the rest of the company: IHOP (filed separately, positive) is the other half of system sales.

findings.finding: Black Box's casual-dining benchmark for June-August 2026 (cited on Darden's 2026-09-24 call) was +2.4% same-restaurant sales with traffic -0.2%, much better than Q1 2026 (full-service visits -2.4% per Placer.ai) and Black Box's -1.2% / -3.0% traffic in Darden's prior quarter — the industry tape under Applebee's improved during Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not observable separately; Q3 2025 (Applebee's +3.1% in a better industry tape) bought +3.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: Industry proxy, partly priced through the sector rally; Applebee's has underperformed Black Box (Q2: -1.8% vs a positive category per DIN's 10-Q), so transmission is uncertain. Proxy, sized small.
findings.independence: Darden release and secondary analysis: https://finviz.com/news/395084/darden-restaurants-reports-fiscal-2027-first-quarter-results-declares-quarterly-dividend-and-reaffirms-fiscal-2027-outlook ; DIN 10-Q says Black Box casual dining was positive in Q2 on check: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000049754/000162828026052924/din-20260628.htm

findings.finding: IHOP laps a -1.5% Q3 2025 comp after +1.5% in Q2 2026 and what management called a third consecutive quarter of industry outperformance on sales and traffic, so an IHOP comp at or above the top of its 0-2% guide is plausible and offsets Applebee's.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026, when IHOP +1.5% offset Applebee's -1.8%, the stock rose +2.58%.
findings.why_not_priced: Easy lap is visible to anyone reading the year-ago release; inside the company's guide, so mostly expected. Sized small.

findings.finding: Applebee's commodity costs rose 8.2% in Q2 2026 on beef, and company-restaurant exposure grew sharply with the June 2026 purchase of 48 Applebee's in FL/GA/AL (plus 12 in VA/NC in February), so Q3 is the first full quarter of a larger company-restaurant base carrying beef inflation; royalties already fell to $77.0M from $82.1M in Q2 as franchised units became company units.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025, when EBITDA fell on company-restaurant remodel and G&A costs, the stock still rose +3.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: Acquisition and commodity figures are in the 10-Q and call, so analysts can model them; what is unknown is the margin on the acquired units. Partly priced, small. The same acquisitions add revenue, which is why print_vs_bar on revenue is positive.
findings.independence: Commodity +8.2% from Q2 call coverage: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/dine-brands-global-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-06/ ; shares the Q2 period with the EBITDA finding but lands on company-restaurant margin, not the guide.

findings.finding: Short interest of ~2.26M shares (~18% of 12.66M shares outstanding, 3.4 days to cover at 2026-09-30, up from 1.8M at 09-15) into a print with a thin, call-heavy option chain (put/call OI 0.09) gives an in-window squeeze mechanism on any acceptable print; the stock is already +18.7% in 20 days, which partly spends it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: an EPS miss ($0.73 vs consensus) with short interest ~18% of float (MarketBeat, 2025-09-15) bought +3.5%; 5 of the last 7 prints rose.
findings.why_not_priced: Short positioning rose into quarter-end while the stock ran, so shorts are underwater and exposed; if they had covered, the 10-15 settlement would show it — it was not found. The run-up may already be the covering, which is why this is small.
